note: Hand-written force structure notes for both sides. Trees are reported public structure with an as-of date and a source; strengths are public estimates naming whose. Commanders link to the public figures roster where a record exists.

items.name: Supreme Commander-in-Chief
items.role: The President of Russia commands the armed forces and, by reporting, intervenes in operational decisions down to brigade level.

items.name: Ministry of Defence
items.role: Political and industrial direction of the war: mobilisation, procurement and the wartime economy. Andrei Belousov, an economist, replaced Sergei Shoigu in May 2024.
items.strength: Russia's declared armed forces ceiling rose to 1.5 million service personnel in 2024 (presidential decree); the deployed force in and around Ukraine is estimated by Ukrainian and Western officials at around 600,000 to 700,000.
items.search: Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation

items.name: General Staff and Joint Grouping of Forces
items.role: Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov has commanded the Joint Grouping of Forces in Ukraine since January 2023, succeeding Sergei Surovikin; he was kept on past retirement age in 2025.

items.name: Groupings of forces
items.role: The front is divided into named groupings, each built on a military district headquarters and several combined-arms armies: North (Kharkiv and Sumy axes), West (Kupiansk and Lyman), South (Siversk and the Donetsk sector), Centre (Pokrovsk and the western Donetsk axis), East (Vuhledar and the Zaporizhzhia boundary) and Dnepr (Zaporizhzhia and Kherson).

items.name: Grouping North
items.role: Formed in 2024 from the Leningrad Military District's forces for the Kharkiv incursion in May 2024, then the defence of Kursk and the Sumy border. Includes the 6th and 11th Armies and the 44th Army Corps.

items.name: Grouping West
items.role: Built on the 1st Guards Tank Army and 20th Combined Arms Army, fighting on the Kupiansk, Lyman and Borova axes in Kharkiv and Luhansk oblasts.

items.name: Grouping Centre
items.role: The Central Military District's forces, including the 2nd and 41st Combined Arms Armies and later the 51st Army (the former 1st Donetsk Corps), which carried the main effort against Avdiivka in 2024 and Pokrovsk in 2024 and 2025.

items.name: Grouping South
items.role: The Southern Military District's 8th Combined Arms Army with the 3rd Army Corps and the former Luhansk corps, responsible for Bakhmut, Chasiv Yar, Toretsk and Siversk.

items.name: Grouping East
items.role: Eastern Military District forces, the 5th, 29th, 35th and 36th Armies, on the Vuhledar and Velyka Novosilka axes at the boundary of Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts.

items.name: Grouping Dnepr
items.role: Holds the Zaporizhzhia front and the left bank of the Dnipro in Kherson with the 58th and 49th Armies and the 18th Army, facing the Ukrainian bridgeheads and the Orikhiv axis.

items.name: Airborne Forces (VDV)
items.role: The 7th, 76th, 98th and 106th divisions and separate brigades, used as the mobile reserve and in the heaviest fighting from Hostomel in 2022 to Kursk in 2024 and 2025. Losses have been heavy and units were rebuilt with mobilised soldiers.
items.strength: Pre-war establishment around 45,000; expanded on paper with new regiments.

items.name: Naval Infantry
items.role: The 155th, 40th, 61st and 810th brigades of the fleets' naval infantry, converted to divisions on paper from 2024, fought at Mariupol, Vuhledar and Kursk with repeated heavy losses.

items.name: Aerospace Forces (VKS)
items.role: Fighters, Su-34 bombers, the Long-Range Aviation bombers that fire cruise missiles, and the air defence forces. Missile Troops and Artillery and the Iskander brigades sit with the ground forces.

items.name: Black Sea Fleet
items.role: Headquartered in Sevastopol until strikes and naval drones forced most ships to Novorossiysk; still launches Kalibr missiles and holds the Kerch Strait.

items.name: Rosgvardia and Akhmat
items.role: The National Guard occupies and polices captured territory and fields its own combat units; the Chechen Akhmat formations, formally within Rosgvardia, took Wagner's assault role in some sectors after 2023.

items.name: Storm-Z and Storm-V penal units
items.role: Assault units of recruited prisoners attached to regular formations, successors to Wagner's prison recruitment, used for costly infantry attacks along the Donetsk front.

items.name: North Korean contingent
items.role: Around 11,000 to 12,000 Korean People's Army troops deployed to Kursk Oblast from late 2024, engaged from November 2024 and reinforced in 2025; North Korea also supplies shells, missiles and guns. Numbers are South Korean, Ukrainian and US estimates.
items.strength: South Korean intelligence estimated 11,000 deployed by early 2025 plus reinforcements; casualties in the thousands.
items.search: North Korean involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine

items.name: Supreme Commander-in-Chief
items.role: The President of Ukraine commands the armed forces through the Staff of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief.

items.name: Ministry of Defence
items.role: Procurement, mobilisation policy and the defence industry; the ministry changed hands several times during the war and its leadership was contested in the 2026 command crisis.
items.strength: Ukraine's armed forces number around one million personnel of whom a few hundred thousand serve in combat units, by official statements; exact figures are not published.

items.name: Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces
items.role: Oleksandr Syrskyi replaced Valerii Zaluzhnyi in February 2024 and was himself replaced by Mykhailo Drapatyi in July 2026 amid a military leadership crisis (reported structure; confirm against current reporting).
items.search: Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

items.name: General Staff
items.role: Plans operations and publishes the daily loss claims shown on this page; the Chief of the General Staff post changed hands with the 2024 and 2026 command changes.
items.search: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

items.name: Ground Forces
items.role: The largest service: mechanised, motorised, tank, artillery and territorial units. In 2025 brigades were grouped into around 18 army corps in a reform intended to fix the span of control of the earlier operational-tactical groups.

items.name: Army corps (2025 reform)
items.role: Corps formed around experienced brigades, including the 1st Azov Corps of the National Guard, the 3rd Army Corps built on the 3rd Assault Brigade, and corps built on the 12th, 53rd and other brigades, each holding a sector with attached artillery and drone units.

items.name: Operational groupings
items.role: Regional joint commands over the corps: the eastern grouping (Donetsk and Luhansk fronts, formerly Khortytsia), the southern grouping (Zaporizhzhia and Kherson, formerly Tavria and Dnipro), the Kursk grouping of 2024 and 2025, and the northern border groupings for Sumy and Kharkiv.

items.name: Air Assault Forces
items.role: Ukraine's elite light infantry brigades (25th, 79th, 80th, 82nd, 95th and others), used as the fire brigade of the front from Hostomel to Kursk.

items.name: Unmanned Systems Forces
items.role: A separate branch created in 2024 for drone units, with dedicated strike regiments such as Magyar's Birds and Achilles that publish confirmed hits; drones now account for the majority of claimed Russian equipment losses.

items.name: Air Force
items.role: Fighters (MiG-29, Su-27, F-16, Mirage 2000), Su-24 and Su-25 strike aircraft, and the anti-aircraft missile forces that operate Patriot, SAMP/T, NASAMS and IRIS-T; publishes the nightly interception figures.

items.name: Navy and Marines
items.role: Coastal missile batteries, naval drones, small boats and the marine corps brigades that fought at Mariupol and hold the Dnipro delta.

items.name: Territorial Defence Forces
items.role: Regional brigades raised in 2022 from volunteers, now fighting as regular infantry across the front; many have been rebuilt several times.

items.name: Special Operations Forces
items.role: Raiding, sabotage and long-range reconnaissance inside occupied territory and Russia, alongside Defence Intelligence's own units and naval drone crews.

items.name: National Guard and Border Guard
items.role: Interior ministry forces that fight as line units: the National Guard's 1st Azov Corps and other brigades, and the State Border Guard Service's assault units in Kharkiv and Sumy.

items.name: Defence Intelligence (HUR)
items.role: The military intelligence directorate runs naval drones, deep strikes and special units and is a frequent source of the claims in this page's updates; treat its statements as an interested party's.
items.search: Chief Directorate of Intelligence of the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine

items.name: Military districts
items.role: The administrative chain that raises, mans and equips the force, separate from the operational groupings that fight the war. The Western Military District was split back into the Moscow and Leningrad districts in 2024, restoring the five-district layout of the Soviet period.

items.name: Leningrad Military District
items.role: Recreated in 2024 out of the Western district, with headquarters in St Petersburg. It generates the forces used on the Kharkiv and Sumy axes and faces the Finnish and Baltic borders after NATO's northern enlargement.

items.name: Moscow Military District
items.role: The second half of the 2024 split of the Western district, covering central Russia and the force generation behind the Kupiansk and Lyman axes.

items.name: Southern Military District
items.role: Headquartered in Rostov-on-Don, the district that has run the war in Donbas since 2014 and administers occupied Crimea and the southern occupied areas.

items.name: Central Military District
items.role: Headquartered in Yekaterinburg; its armies have carried the main effort on the Avdiivka and Pokrovsk axes since 2023.

items.name: Eastern Military District
items.role: Headquartered in Khabarovsk; its armies were moved west in 2022 and have fought on the southern Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia boundary ever since.

items.name: 6th Combined Arms Army
items.role: A Leningrad district army committed to the Kharkiv incursion of May 2024 and then to holding the Russian side of the Sumy and Kharkiv border.

items.name: 1st Guards Tank Army
items.role: Russia's showpiece armoured army before 2022. It lost much of its equipment in the Kharkiv collapse of September 2022, was rebuilt with mobilised soldiers and now fights as ordinary infantry-heavy formations on the Kupiansk axis.

items.name: 8th Guards Combined Arms Army
items.role: The Southern district army that absorbed the former Luhansk and Donetsk corps units and fought the long battles for Bakhmut, Chasiv Yar and Toretsk.

items.name: 51st Combined Arms Army
items.role: Formed in 2023 from the 1st Army Corps, the former Donetsk separatist force, and folded into the regular army. It fought at Avdiivka and on the Pokrovsk axis.

items.name: 58th Combined Arms Army
items.role: Holds the Zaporizhzhia front that absorbed Ukraine's 2023 counter-offensive. Its commander Ivan Popov was dismissed in July 2023 after complaining publicly about counter-battery losses and the treatment of his soldiers.

items.name: Main Directorate of the General Staff (GRU)
items.role: Military intelligence: agent networks, the Spetsnaz brigades, deep reconnaissance, and the sabotage campaign in Europe that European security services have attributed to it.

items.name: Spetsnaz brigades
items.role: The 2nd, 3rd, 10th, 14th, 16th and 22nd special purpose brigades. Western and Ukrainian reporting says they were used as assault infantry from 2022 and rebuilt repeatedly after heavy losses, well outside their reconnaissance role.

items.name: Africa Corps
items.role: The Ministry of Defence structure that took over most of Wagner's African deployments after Yevgeny Prigozhin's death in August 2023, reported to run under General Staff and GRU direction. It fights in the Sahel and Libya rather than in Ukraine, but it absorbed Wagner's people and contracts.
items.strength: Western and regional reporting put it in the low thousands across Mali, Libya, Burkina Faso and Niger during 2024 and 2025; no official figure is published.

items.name: Redut and company formations
items.role: Ministry of Defence-linked contractor structures, Redut chief among them, that recruited Wagner veterans after the 2023 mutiny, alongside state-company units such as Gazprom's Potok. They fight as assault units under regular commanders.

items.name: Rubicon centre for unmanned systems
items.role: A drone centre created on the defence minister's order in 2024 to concentrate the best crews, training and equipment. Ukrainian and Western reporting through 2025 described its detachments as the most effective Russian drone units, deployed to Kursk and to the Pokrovsk axis to hunt Ukrainian logistics.
items.search: Rubicon Center of Advanced Unmanned Technologies

items.name: Long-Range Aviation
items.role: The bomber force, Tu-95MS, Tu-160 and Tu-22M3, that launches the cruise missiles in the mass strikes on the power grid and cities. Its home bases, deep inside Russia, have been struck repeatedly by Ukrainian drones, including the June 2025 operation against aircraft parked at several airfields.

items.name: Missile Troops and Artillery
items.role: The ground forces' artillery arm, including the Iskander brigades that fire the ballistic and cruise missiles used against cities and airfields.

items.name: Akhmat formations
items.role: Chechen units raised under Ramzan Kadyrov, formally inside Rosgvardia and the Ministry of Defence, used for assaults, for blocking detachments behind other units and heavily for publicity. Apty Alaudinov, their public commander, also holds a political post in the Ministry of Defence.

items.name: Federal Security Service (FSB)
items.role: Holds the state border with its Border Service, runs counter-sabotage in the border oblasts and places military counter-intelligence officers inside formations. It reports to the president, not to the Ministry of Defence.

items.name: Eastern grouping of forces
items.role: The joint command for the Donetsk and Luhansk fronts, previously named Khortytsia. It holds the Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, Siversk and Lyman axes, the heaviest fighting of the war since 2023.

items.name: Southern grouping of forces
items.role: The joint command for Zaporizhzhia, Kherson and the Dnipro line, built from the earlier Tavriia and Odesa commands. It also covers the Black Sea coast and the Kinburn spit.

items.name: Northern grouping of forces
items.role: Covers Sumy, Chernihiv and northern Kharkiv, the border raids of 2024 and the Kursk operation begun in August 2024, which Russian and North Korean forces largely reversed through the spring of 2025.

items.name: 3rd Army Corps
items.role: Built in 2025 around the 3rd Assault Brigade, the formation raised by Andrii Biletskyi from the original Azov Regiment's veterans. It holds part of the Kharkiv and Lyman sector and recruits publicly on its own account.

items.name: 1st Azov Corps (National Guard)
items.role: The National Guard corps formed in 2025 around the 12th Azov Brigade, the successor to the Mariupol garrison. It is a National Guard formation that fights under whichever operational grouping holds its sector.

items.name: 414th Magyar's Birds Brigade
items.role: The strike drone formation founded by Robert Brovdi, call sign Magyar, which grew from a volunteer unit into the 414th brigade and publishes counted strikes. Brovdi was appointed to command the Unmanned Systems Forces in 2025.

items.name: 429th Achilles Regiment
items.role: A strike drone unit grown out of a battalion of the 92nd Brigade into a regiment and then a brigade-sized formation, working the Kharkiv and Donetsk axes and known for publishing verified strike footage.

items.name: Marine Corps
items.role: The marine brigades, raised to a corps command in 2023, which fought at Mariupol, held the Krynky bridgehead on the left bank of the Dnipro through 2024 and were committed to the Kursk operation.

items.name: Air commands and anti-aircraft missile brigades
items.role: The four regional air commands, Centre, West, South and East, with the anti-aircraft missile brigades, radar brigades and the mobile fire groups that shoot down Shahed-type drones over the cities.

items.name: Support and logistics forces
items.role: Engineering, explosive ordnance disposal, chemical defence, movement and supply, plus the Medical Forces. Demining alone is a decades-long task: Ukraine is among the most heavily mined countries in the world by United Nations and government statements.
items.search: Logistics Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

items.name: Territorial recruitment centres
items.role: The conscription and mobilisation offices. Recruitment practice became a public scandal in 2023 to 2025, with corruption cases against centre officials and widely reported complaints about street conscription; mobilisation shortfalls are a recurring theme in Ukrainian and Western reporting.

items.name: Security Service of Ukraine (SBU)
items.role: Counter-intelligence and internal security, with its own combat and special operations units: the Alpha special centre, drone units of its 13th directorate and the Sea Baby naval drone programme used against the Kerch bridge and Black Sea Fleet ships.

items.name: HUR special units
items.role: Defence Intelligence's own formations, including Tymur, Artan, Shaman, Prymary and the Russian-manned Freedom of Russia and Russian Volunteer Corps units, used for raids into Russia, Crimea and occupied territory.
